plan.title: bug(hooks): .githooks run_deft prefers a stale global deft over the fresh local CLI in a framework-source checkout (new verbs block commits)

narratives.Description: In a framework-source (monorepo) checkout, the git hooks' shared resolver .githooks/_deft-run.sh prefers a global `deft` on PATH over the freshly-built local CLI (packages/cli/dist/bin.js). When a PR adds a new verb (e.g. verify:forward-coverage from #1310), the stale global CLI does not know the verb and the hook fails with `directive: unknown verb '<verb>'`, blocking commits/pushes until the operator manually refreshes the global install.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer committing in the framework-source monorepo, I want the git hooks to invoke the freshly-built local CLI (which always has the current verb set) rather than a stale global `deft`, so a newly-added-and-wired verb does not block my commits after `task build`.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. In .githooks/_deft-run.sh, change run_deft resolution so that in a framework-source checkout (detectable via `packages/cli/dist/bin.js` existing under $REPO_ROOT, or another monorepo marker) the LOCAL built CLI is preferred over a global `deft`. 2. Consumer installs (vendored .deft/core with no local build) must keep resolving the global `deft` exactly as today -- do not regress the consumer path. 3. Add a DEFT_HOOKS_PREFER_GLOBAL=1 escape hatch to force the global for the rare inverse case. 4. This is a shell-script change; the recurrence bit BOTH swarm workers and the finalize-cohort commit in the #2249-#2255 cohort, each needing a manual /tmp shim -- eliminate that tax. 5. Add coverage: a test (bats-style or a TS harness that execs the script under a temp fake-global on PATH + a temp REPO_ROOT with/without dist/bin.js) asserting local-preferred-when-dist-present, global-preferred-when-no-dist, and DEFT_HOOKS_PREFER_GLOBAL override. 6. Run repo-root pnpm run lint (full-file lane) + task check.
narratives.Overview: See https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/2248. .githooks/_deft-run.sh's run_deft does `if command -v deft; then deft "$@"; elif [ -f dist/bin.js ]; then node dist/bin.js ...`. Global always wins when present, even in a maintainer monorepo where the local build is authoritative and fresher for verb coverage. Fix: prefer local build in framework-source checkouts; keep global for consumers; add an escape hatch.
narratives.GuardRails: Do NOT break the consumer (vendored .deft/core) resolution path -- consumers have no local build and MUST keep using the global. Detect framework-source via a stable marker (existing dist/bin.js under $REPO_ROOT and/or a monorepo sentinel like pnpm-workspace.yaml), not a brittle heuristic. Keep the freeze-gate happy (this is not Go installer code). Preserve exit codes so hook pass/fail semantics are unchanged.

items.title: In a framework-source checkout with a built packages/cli/dist/bin.js, the hooks invoke the local CLI (new verbs work without refreshing the global).
Consumer installs (no local build) still resolve the global `deft` exactly as before.
A newly-added verb wired into a hook does not block commits in the monorepo after `task build`.
DEFT_HOOKS_PREFER_GLOBAL=1 escape hatch forces the global resolution.
Regression coverage exercises local-preferred, consumer-global, and the override.
